figures.caption: Fig. 1. Personalized federated framework of PFedHASNet. The server aggregates the shared encoder, while each client retains local EEG, a private residual adapter, and a private classifier for personalized local training.

Fig. 2. Architecture of PFedHASNet. (a) Multi-scale spatiotemporal feature extraction backbone. (b) HASR, which integrates a continuous-valued summary, LIF spike rates, and channel-wise LogVar statistics. (c) Client-private residual adapter and private classifier.

TABLE III SAME-BACKBONE COMPARISON: (A) MEAN-CLIENT MACRO-AVERAGED F1 SCORE (%, MEAN ± SAMPLE SD ACROSS THREE SEEDS); (B) TRAINING PROTOCOLS AND NOMINAL COSTS. FEDERATED METHODS A–G USE 100 ROUNDS; CENTRAL AND LOCAL USE 200 EPOCHS.

TABLE II CROSS-MODEL MEAN-CLIENT MACRO-F1 (%; MEAN ± SAMPLE SD ACROSS THREE SEEDS) AT ROUND 100. AVERAGE AND MEAN RANK SUMMARIZE FOUR DATASETS; BOLD AND UNDERLINING MARK THE BEST AND SECOND-BEST MEANS.

Fig. 3. Module ablations at round 100 (µ = 0.0006). (a) Full-minus-ablated mean-client test macro-F1 (pp) on M1–M4. (b) Adapter gains for seeds 42, 2026, and 3407; diamonds and whiskers show mean ± sample SD. Ablations remove the LogVar branch or private residual adapter, respectively; the latter retains the private classifier.

Fig. 4. Matched 2 × 2 LIF–personalization ablation at round 100 (µ = 0), with the analog and LogVar branches retained. Bars show meanclient test macro-F1 (%) across three seeds, with sample SD error bars. The four LIF–personalization configurations are compared on M1–M4. Conditional gains and interactions are reported in Table V.

TABLE V CONDITIONAL PERSONALIZATION AND LIF GAINS IN THE MATCHED 2 × 2 FACTORIAL ABLATION AT ROUND 100 (µ = 0). VALUES ARE WITHIN-SEED PAIRED MEAN ± SAMPLE SD ACROSS SEEDS 42, 2026, AND 3407 (PP). THE INTERACTION I IS THE COMMON DIFFERENCE OF DIFFERENCES FOR THE TWO FACTORS.

Fig. 5. Client-level personalization gains at round 100 (LIF on, µ = 0). Bars show mean paired personalization on–off differences in test macro-F1 across seeds 42, 2026, and 3407 (pp); whiskers indicate seed-wise minima and maxima, not SDs or confidence intervals. Blue and yellow denote positive and negative mean gains, respectively.

Fig. 6. Post-aggregation mean-client test macro-F1 (%) on M1–M4 for six configurations. Curves and shading show mean ± sample SD across three seeds; enlarged markers indicate round 100. Hybrid denotes Hybrid-FedAvg.

Fig. 7. Within-round aggregation effects on mean-client test macro-F1. (a) Mean post−pre change (MeanAgg, pp), with a zero-centered scale. (b) Frequency of strictly negative changes (%; scale 0–100). Each cell summarizes three seeds × 100 rounds.
